g.text: Introduction to OSHA: Lesson 1: Introduction to OSHA (AI-written scenario, guide-sourced answer)
You are walking through the warehouse and notice a worker reaching into a drum labeled "Chemical" without
gloves. You hear a loud noise from the direction of the loading dock, and when you check, you see a forklift
operator has just dropped a pallet. The noise level near the loading area is around 85 dB. A worker mentions
they saw a spill earlier but didn’t report it. What applies here, and what do you do first, second, and third?
An example of an OSHA standard is 29 CFR 1910.95, which involves occupational noise exposure.
Under OSHA's standard 1910.1020, every employee has the right to examine and copy exposure
and medical records, including records of workplace monitoring or measuring a toxic substance.
OSHA requires hearing conservation programs to be in place where noise is present in a workplace,
particularly when the noise level exceeds the 85 dB TWA.
All work-related inpatient hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye must be reported to
If you believe you have been punished for exercising your rights, you must contact OSHA within 30
days to preserve the protections provided under the OSH Act.
Then, a CSHO would perform an inspection within 24 hours of receiving the report.
